objects.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
objects.description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system to initially access a network. Vulnerabilities such as SQL injection, remote code execution, or path traversal in a web application are common entry points.

objects.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
objects.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters (e.g. a shell, PowerShell, Python) to execute commands, scripts, or binaries, often after achieving code execution via an injection vulnerability in an application.

objects.name: Unsecured Credentials
objects.description: Adversaries may search compromised systems, source code, configuration files, or environment variables to find credentials such as hard-coded passwords, API keys, or private keys stored in plaintext.

objects.name: Valid Accounts
objects.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts, including those exposed via weak authentication, credential stuffing, or reused/default passwords, as a means of gaining access while evading detection.

objects.name: Application Layer Protocol
objects.description: Adversaries may communicate using OSI application layer protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, DNS) to blend command-and-control traffic with existing traffic, often exploiting an SSRF vulnerability to reach internal-only endpoints.

objects.name: Process Injection
objects.description: Adversaries may inject code into processes in order to evade process-based defenses and elevate privileges, sometimes achieved via a deserialization vulnerability that allows arbitrary code execution in the target process.

objects.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
objects.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability, often after gaining code execution through an application vulnerability, as part of a ransomware operation.

objects.name: Supply Chain Compromise
objects.description: Adversaries may manipulate products or product delivery mechanisms, such as third-party software dependencies, before receipt by a final consumer, to achieve data or system compromise - relevant when an application uses vulnerable or outdated components.

objects.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
objects.description: Adversaries may exploit remote services (e.g. a database, RPC endpoint, or internal API reachable via SSRF) to gain unauthorized access, often by taking advantage of a programming error such as a buffer overflow or injection flaw.

objects.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
objects.description: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevated privileges, exploiting broken access control or improper authorization checks in an application to gain higher-privileged access than intended.

objects.name: Escape to Host
objects.description: Adversaries may break out of a container to gain access to the underlying host, sometimes made possible by a path traversal or deserialization vulnerability in a containerized application combined with an overly permissive container configuration.

objects.name: Endpoint Denial of Service
objects.description: Adversaries may perform attacks that degrade or block the availability of a targeted resource, for example by exploiting an unbounded resource-consumption flaw (e.g. XML entity expansion, unvalidated file uploads) in an application endpoint.
